newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka stocks end 6.81 pct down on panic selling.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka stocks end 6.81 pct down on panic selling.

text.p: Dhaka stocks slid nearly seven percent at close after investors, panicked by rumour that a government enquiry may implicate some big brokers in market manipulation, dumped shares, brokers said.

The benchmark price index of the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) fell 78.57 points or 6.81 percent at 1,074.95. Of 118 traded issues, 110 lost, seven gained and one unchanged. Tunrover slumped to 49.8 million taka from Monday's 70.6 million.
A enquiry committee, appointed by the government, is due to submit a report on Thursday on alledged manipulation of share prices during October-November bull-run and sharp fall later.
"The investors were also worried about the possible impact of the committee's finding in the report," said broker Shahidullah Shamoyl.
Brokers said the trading also suffered amid noisy agitation by traders in the kerb market protesting the heavy fall in share prices.
Monno Fabrics lost 2.14 taka to 136.27 and Beximco Pharma shed 15.25 to 137.25. The market will remain closed on Wednesday for independence day holiday.
